topic: Introduction and basic principles, classification of surveys
source: survey1-100 / 101-175 / 175-250 / 251-350 / 350-455 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

options: to work from whole to the part
to work from part to whole
questions.explain: This is a fundamental principle to prevent the accumulation of errors and to localize them within a specific area.

questions.q: 2. Under Survey 'working from whole to part' is done:
options: to prevent the accumulation of error
questions.explain: By establishing a large primary control network first, errors made in smaller, subsequent measurements do not affect the overall framework.

questions.q: 3. The curvature of the earth's surface is taken into account only if the extent of survey is more than:
questions.explain: In plane surveying, the earth is considered flat. If the area exceeds approximately 250-260 sq km, the curvature must be considered (Geodetic Surveying).

questions.q: 4. Geodetic survey is different from plane surveying because of:
options: the curvature of the earth is considered
questions.explain: While large areas are a reason to use it, the technical definition of geodetic surveying is that it accounts for the earth's spherical shape.

questions.q: 5. The limitation for geodetic survey is:
questions.explain: Generally, if the survey area is less than 250 km², plane surveying is used. Beyond this limit, geodetic methods are required.

questions.q: 6. Hydrographic survey deal with the mapping of:
questions.explain: Hydrographic surveys are conducted to map shorelines, depths of water bodies (oceans, lakes, rivers), and under-water features.

questions.q: 7. The survey which is carried out for determining absolute locations and the direction of any line... by making observation to heavenly bodies is called:
questions.explain: This uses observations of the sun or stars to determine absolute azimuth (direction), latitude, and longitude.

questions.q: 27. Which one is the simplest survey ?
questions.explain: It is the simplest form of surveying because it only requires linear measurements (no angles) and basic equipment like a chain and arrows.

questions.q: 28. During geodetic survey which one is considered:
options: mass of the earth is considered
questions.explain: In geodetic surveying, the earth's surface is treated as a spheroid, so lines are arcs and triangles are spherical triangles.

questions.q: 29. Cadastral Map is a map having:
questions.explain: Cadastral maps show property boundaries, house numbers, and land ownership. To show these details accurately, a large scale (e.g., 1/500 to 1/2500) is required.

questions.q: 30. In city for planning, plotting the details as well as property line is:
questions.explain: These are specific legal maps used for tax purposes and to define the boundaries of individual land parcels in a city or village.

questions.q: 445. Which one of the following wrongly describes plane surveying?:
options: it refers to a flat plane without considering curvature of the earth
it ignores the actual shape of the earth
it is performed on the surface of the earth
it considers the size and shape of the earth
questions.explain: This wrongly describes plane surveying; Geodetic surveying is the branch that considers the size and shape (curvature) of the earth. Plane surveying specifically assumes the earth is flat.

questions.q: 450. A systematic process for combining opinions into a reasoned consensus is:
questions.explain: The Delphi method is a structured communication technique used to reach a reasoned consensus among a panel of experts through multiple rounds of questioning.
